models._description: stock_delivery declares 0 own _name models; it is a pure extension/bridge of 13 inherit-only models that wires the delivery.carrier abstraction into stock.picking / stock.move execution.
Stock Move - weight + carrier propagation on picking assignment
Move Line - sale_price/hs_code/country for customs + put-in-pack
Packaging - shipping weight, weight UoM, package_carrier_type, shipper_package_code
Carrier selection wizard - real-cost invoicing message
propagate carrier to pending pickings on set_delivery_line; carrier route_ids into procurement

behavioral_notes.observation: This is the bridge's core act. button_validate -> _send_confirmation_email iterates the pickings and, when pick.carrier_id.integration_level == 'rate_and_ship' and the type is not 'incoming' and there is no carrier_tracking_ref yet and picking_type_id.print_label, calls pick.sudo().send_to_shipper(). send_to_shipper calls self.carrier_id.send_shipping(self)[0] (the reflective '<delivery_type>_send_shipping' dispatch defined in the delivery module), applies free_over zeroing and carrier margins to set carrier_price, writes res['tracking_number'] back into carrier_tracking_ref across the up/down-stream related pickings, posts a chatter message with cost+tracking, and calls _add_delivery_cost_to_so. A carrier UserError after at least one picking was already shipped is downgraded to a chatter note + a 'warning' activity instead of rolling back the whole validate batch. Not visible in metadata (cross-module side-effect on a related Selection value).

carrier_tracking_ref is the stored tracking number returned by the carrier; carrier_tracking_url is computed via carrier_id.get_tracking_link(picking) (reflective '<type>_get_tracking_link'; the built-in fixed/base_on_rule providers substitute the ref into the carrier tracking_url template). open_website_url opens the courier tracking page (single URL) or, for JSON multi-tracker payloads, posts the links to chatter and opens the trackers action. The base 'delivery' module deliberately holds NO stock.picking model, so these tracking fields and the send-to-shipper behaviour exist only here.

cancel_shipment loops the pickings, calls carrier_id.cancel_shipment(self) (reflective '<type>_cancel_shipment'; the base fixed/base_on_rule providers raise NotImplementedError), posts a cancellation chatter message and clears carrier_tracking_ref. _add_delivery_cost_to_so closes the loop to Quote-to-Cash: when carrier_id.invoice_policy == 'real', it locates the zero-priced delivery line on sale_id (or _create_delivery_line) and writes the actual carrier_price back onto the sale.order.line under the allow_delivery_cost_update context, so the customer is billed the real shipped cost rather than the estimate.

behavioral_notes.element: carrier propagation across chained pickings (stock.move._get_new_picking_values / _key_assign_picking / stock.picking.button_validate)
behavioral_notes.observation: When a move's rule_id has propagate_carrier, _get_new_picking_values copies carrier_id (and carrier_tracking_ref) from the originating sale.order or the previous picking onto a newly-created picking, and _key_assign_picking adds carrier_id to the picking-grouping key so moves with different carriers split into different transfers. After validation, button_validate also pushes carrier_id + carrier_tracking_ref onto the next transfers (_get_next_transfers) when the propagate_carrier rule applies, keeping the carrier consistent across push/pull (pick-pack-ship) multi-step routes.

Putting move lines in a pack threads carrier context: _pre_put_in_pack_hook injects default_package_carrier_type via _get_package_carrier_type_for_pack (which forbids mixing different carriers in one package and maps the built-in 'fixed'/'base_on_rule' delivery_type to 'none'); the stock.put.in.pack wizard computes shipping_weight (product weights + package base_weight) and warns when it exceeds the package type's max_weight; _post_put_in_pack_hook stamps the chosen shipping_weight onto the package. stock.package.type adds shipper_package_code (carrier's package code, defaulted from carrier._get_default_custom_package_code) so custom packaging maps to the carrier's catalogue.

No static frontend assets: extract_frontend reports present=false, 0 JS files, 0 XML templates, 0 OWL components/registry adds/patches/services and no asset bundles. The module is server-side only (Python extensions + 14 backend data/report XML files); the carrier-picker UX (LocationSelectorDialog, Map, etc.) lives in the base 'delivery' module, not here.

external_integrations.character: carrier-execution bridge (gap #7 boundary): this module invokes the delivery.carrier send/track/cancel SPI at picking validate time but makes no external call itself. The built-in fixed/base_on_rule providers it ships against return stub data (tracking_number=False, cancel raises NotImplementedError); real outbound carrier API traffic (FedEx/UPS/DHL/Easypost/Sendcloud) lives in delivery_* connector sub-modules that implement '<type>_send_shipping'. uses_api_keys=true reflects credential/sandbox plumbing surfaced through delivery.carrier (prod_environment/integration_level).

classification.rationale: stock_delivery is the bridge that realizes the outbound-logistics carrier-execution leg of the value chain, so its value_model is chain. It is THE BRIDGE delivery <-> stock that the base 'delivery' module deliberately deferred: 'delivery' provides the delivery.carrier abstraction (rate/ship/track/cancel SPI) but has no stock dependency and no stock.picking model, while 'stock' performs the physical transfer; this auto_install module (on sale_stock + delivery) is where the two meet - it wires carrier_id onto stock.picking and, at button_validate, actually executes send_to_shipper -> delivery.carrier.send_shipping, captures carrier_tracking_ref, and feeds the real shipping cost back into Quote-to-Cash. It is classed as a support activity because it provisions/operates the shipping capability for the chain (it dispatches to the carrier SPI and orchestrates packing/tracking/invoicing) rather than being the primary order-fulfilment activity itself; the concrete external carrier API call is still delegated to delivery_* connector sub-modules (gap #7). APQC maps to 4.4 Operate outbound transportation / ship (Supply Chain), matching apqc_odoo_map.tsv row '4.4.x Operate outbound transportation (ship) -> stock.picking button_validate (delivery)'.
